correctness.rationale: For a connected simple unicyclic graph, a nonzero principal Pfaffian of order 2ν(S) exists whenever the induced matching on its endpoints is unique. Distinct perfect matchings can differ only on the sole full even cycle. With the cycle fully supported, let a_v=ν(T_v−v), b_v=ν(T_v); b_v−a_v∈{0,1}. If every b_v=a_v, all maximum matchings stay off cycle-to-tree edges, their maximal Pfaffians share the same two-monomial even-cycle binomial Δ_C. If some b_v=a_v+1, a maximal matching using a cycle-to-tree edge yields a unique-monomial nonzero Pfaffian. Each exceptional support has exactly one in q−1 nonzero cycle-weight assignments satisfying Δ_C=0, and deleting one cycle matching edge gives a nonzero Pfaffian of order 2ν−2, so the drop is exactly two, including char2. Summing support counts proves R_G=H_G(q−1,z)+(q−1)^(ℓ−1) z^(ℓ/2−1)(1−z)∏_v Q_v(q−1,z) for even ℓ, and R_G=H_G for odd ℓ. O’Brien–Voll/Rossmann char rank conversion gives the ordinary character-degree formula for odd q only. Independent direct Gaussian elimination for a four-cycle with pendant length-two path gives q2 ranks [1,15,36,12], q3 [1,56,384,288], matching the factorized formula; not a universal proof.
residual_risks: Finite connected simple exactly-unicyclic graphs; not cactus/multicyclic or multigraph.
Rank enumeration valid all finite fields; character-degree conversion asserted only odd q.
